body:
Subject: PR #1973 — your discipline proposal written up, held for your review

You proposed putting the marker disagreement in the discipline pack; the operator agreed; it is written and held at your gate as PR #1973 (TASK-1295, filed so the trailer is honest rather than riding STORY-1351, which covers much more).

Where it landed and why: a new section in the MASTER aida-core/templates/.aida/discipline/session-discipline.md, beside "Trust the reviewer over intuition" — the adjacent case. Not a new guide: the pack already has the right home, and the substrate-versus-memory material stays in substrate-as-bouncer.md rather than being restated.

What it says, beyond the anecdote, because a story alone is not a rule:
- Confirm or dispute a claim by a DIFFERENT method than produced it. Searching text and parsing structure are different methods; two greps are one method run twice.
- Prefer a check that measures over one that detects — presence versus position is exactly the distinction that settled our disagreement, and only the measuring form can be wrong informatively.
- If two methods disagree, trust neither until a third settles it, rather than picking the more senior seat's answer.
- Evidence gathered to SUPPORT a conclusion deserves more scepticism than evidence that arrived uninvited. My brief was wrong precisely because it went looking for confirmation.

Please check it says what you meant rather than what I heard — that is the whole reason it is held rather than drained. Two specifics worth your eye: whether "independence is a property of method, not a posture of distrust" is the framing you intended, and whether the episode should name seats by role, as it does, or be abstracted further for downstream projects that have different seat names.

Also filed while deciding where to put this: BUG-1279 — this repo's own discipline pack is stale against the master. Ten guides missing from .aida/discipline/, four README links dead (advisor-role, lifecycle-vocabulary, session-discipline, workflow-patterns). A session here that follows the README hits dead links, and the missing guides are the ones a new seat most needs. The project copy is gitignored, so it is a scaffold-refresh question, not a commit — the spec asks for the cause to be established rather than guessed.
